lesson.beat.builds.alt: Seasons two and three. Path A’s skill bars rise faster than before, with arrows showing ball control helping passing and passing helping positioning. Path B’s bars rise slowly.
lesson.beat.builds.body1: Once Path A Maya can control the ball without staring at it, she can look up and see her teammates. That makes passing and positioning easier to learn.
lesson.beat.builds.body2: Each skill gives the next one a place to stand. Path B Maya is still working on the basics, so the gap grows.
lesson.beat.builds.heading: Then learning builds on learning.
lesson.beat.closed.alt: Rain clouds over the ridge. The lake trail beyond the bridge is marked closed. A ranger stands at the bridge.
lesson.beat.closed.body1: Last night’s storm washed out part of the lake trail. A ranger at the bridge says it’s closed. All their planning couldn’t stop the rain.
lesson.beat.closed.heading: Something they couldn’t control.
lesson.beat.closed.option.ask: Ask the ranger about other trails
lesson.beat.closed.option.ask.feedback: The ranger points to the Waterfall Trail. It’s shorter, and it’s open.
lesson.beat.closed.option.home.feedback: Feeling disappointed is normal—Alfredo feels it too, and going home would be allowed. But is there another good option?
lesson.beat.closed.option.sneak.feedback: The sign is there because the trail isn’t safe. Ignoring it could turn a disappointing day into a dangerous one.
lesson.beat.cover.alt: A single dot marks the beginning of a life.
lesson.beat.cover.body1: How your choices—and the things you can’t choose—shape where a life can go.
lesson.beat.cover.body2: Go at your own pace. You’ll join a hike, follow one girl down two paths, spend ten afternoons, then explore a life of your own.
lesson.beat.cover.heading: The paths we make
lesson.beat.explore.alt: An interactive map of example life choices. At each fork, two or three labelled choices branch ahead; some are closed with a reason. The chosen path turns dark green, with gray branches for choices not taken.
lesson.beat.explore.body1: Start at the beginning and pick a choice at each fork. Hover a path to see where it could lead. Some ways close for reasons you can’t control. You can always go back.
lesson.beat.explore.heading: Choose a life path.
lesson.beat.fork.alt: One path splits into two lanes. Path A: Maya keeps practising. Path B: Maya mostly skips.
lesson.beat.fork.body1: Meet Maya. She’s eight and has just joined a soccer team.
lesson.beat.fork.body2: Let’s imagine two ways her next three years could go. It’s the same Maya with the same start. Only her choices are different.
lesson.beat.fork.heading: Same start, two paths.
lesson.beat.game.alt: A game of ten afternoons. Each afternoon offers three choices. Skill boxes for soccer and cello, and an energy meter, show what builds up.
lesson.beat.game.body1: You play soccer and you’re learning the cello. You have ten afternoons after school. Each one, choose what to do—and watch what builds up.
lesson.beat.game.body2: Rest counts too. When you’re worn out, practice doesn’t stick as well.
lesson.beat.game.heading: Ten afternoons, two skills.
lesson.beat.halfway.alt: The walkers climb to the big rock. Their water bottles are half full; the lake is still far away.
lesson.beat.halfway.body1: Partway up, Alfredo checks his bottle. Half the water is gone, and the lake is still far away.
lesson.beat.halfway.heading: Halfway through the water.
lesson.beat.halfway.option.continue.feed: They would reach the lake with almost no water left for the long walk home. On a warm day, that could be dangerous. Dad says, “The lake will still be here. Let’s turn back.”
lesson.beat.halfway.option.turn.feedback: Good thinking. The other half of the water is for getting home safely.
lesson.beat.many.alt: Hundreds of green paths branch out from the beginning dot and spread across the map.
lesson.beat.many.body1: Each line is a way a life could go. Lines split, bend and cross. No one walks them all—and no one needs to.
lesson.beat.many.heading: A life has many possible paths.
lesson.beat.never-late.alt: Both Mayas practise basketball for a season. Path B’s calendar fills for the first time and her bars rise; Path A keeps her head start.
lesson.beat.never-late.body1: Path B Maya can start practising any season. When she does, her skills grow too. She has more to build than Path A Maya, but the door isn’t closed.
lesson.beat.never-late.body2: Real life is messier than this picture. Coaches, time, money for a team and luck matter too. Not every skill carries across, and practice doesn’t guarantee a result.
lesson.beat.never-late.heading: It’s never too late to start.
lesson.beat.outside.alt: A few paths ahead are marked closed, with reasons such as a full team or a cancelled class. Many others remain open.
lesson.beat.outside.body1: Other people, the help you have, and luck shape the path too. Some ways close for reasons nobody chose.
lesson.beat.outside.body2: Your choices matter—they’re just not the whole story. Let’s zoom in on one stretch of path.
lesson.beat.outside.heading: Not everything is yours to choose.
lesson.beat.plan.alt: A trail map: the trail climbs from the trailhead through a forest, over a stream and up a ridge to Mirror Lake. Alfredo and his dad wait at the trailhead with full water bottles.
lesson.beat.plan.body1: Alfredo and his dad want to hike to Mirror Lake. They study the map, then pack snacks, jackets and a bottle of water each.
lesson.beat.plan.body2: No single step will get them there. Lots of steps, with rests along the way, can.
lesson.beat.plan.heading: Alfredo makes a plan.
lesson.beat.practice.alt: Three short practice loops appear near home, one after another. The backpack gains three cards: Reading the map, Spotting landmarks, Resting before you’re tired.
lesson.beat.practice.body1: Over the next few weeks they take shorter walks near home. Alfredo practises reading the map and spotting landmarks.
lesson.beat.practice.body2: Each walk starts from what he learned on the last one. His dad still helps—learning with someone counts.
lesson.beat.practice.heading: Practice builds on practice.
lesson.beat.respond.alt: The walkers follow the open Waterfall Trail to a lookout beside a waterfall.
lesson.beat.respond.body1: They take the Waterfall Trail and eat lunch by the falls. The lake can wait—and everything they learned comes with them.
lesson.beat.respond.body2: That’s resilience: not controlling everything, but finding a good way forward.
lesson.beat.respond.closer.body1: No. Turning back, resting, asking for help or choosing a different goal can all be good responses.
lesson.beat.respond.closer.body2: Alfredo can feel disappointed and still decide what to do next. He doesn’t have to pretend the setback feels good.
lesson.beat.respond.closer.heading: Does resilience mean never stopping?
lesson.beat.respond.heading: Plans change. You can respond.
lesson.beat.retry.alt: The walkers climb past the place where they turned back last time, with plenty of water, and reach the bridge over the stream.
lesson.beat.retry.body1: This time they carry more water and plan their rest stops. Alfredo recognises the big rock and the stream from the map.
lesson.beat.retry.body2: They aren’t starting from zero. Everything they learned is coming with them.
lesson.beat.retry.heading: The second try.
lesson.beat.slow.alt: Season one. Path A’s calendar is mostly filled; Path B’s has a few practices. Both sets of skill bars are low, with Path A slightly ahead.
lesson.beat.slow.body1: In her first season, Path A Maya goes to most practices and kicks a ball against the wall at home. Path B Maya goes now and then.
lesson.beat.slow.body2: After one season the difference is small. Early practice often feels like not much is happening.
lesson.beat.slow.heading: At first, progress feels slow.
lesson.beat.sort.alt: Six cards sorted into two groups. Their choices: how much water to pack, turning back, practising with the map, asking the ranger. Outside their control: the storm, the trail closing.
lesson.beat.sort.body1: Sort each card. Was it their choice, or something outside their control?
lesson.beat.sort.heading: What was in their control?
lesson.beat.takeaways.alt: The life map returns, with the traveller at Today and many light green paths still open ahead.
lesson.beat.takeaways.body1: Your choices matter—they’re just not the whole story. The paths ahead are still open. What will you practise next?
lesson.beat.takeaways.heading: What to take with you.
lesson.beat.transfer.alt: Both skill boxes switch to basketball. Path A starts with part of Court sense and Passing already filled, carried across from soccer. Dribbling starts low for both. Path B starts low on all three.
lesson.beat.transfer.body1: At eleven, both Mayas try basketball. It’s a different ball, and dribbling with your hands is new.
lesson.beat.transfer.body2: But Path A Maya already knows where to stand and when to pass—that carries across. Path B Maya has to learn nearly all of it from the start.
lesson.beat.transfer.heading: Trying something new.
lesson.beat.travel.alt: A dot travels from the beginning to Today, age 12. Labels name some choices: dark ones taken along the route, gray ones not taken, and green ones still possible ahead.
lesson.beat.travel.body1: Here’s someone who is twelve. The dark line is their path so far. At each fork they chose one way; the others turned gray.
lesson.beat.travel.body2: Ahead, the green paths are still open. What they learn and practise changes which ones they’re ready for.
lesson.beat.travel.heading: We travel one path at a time.
lesson.beat.turnback.alt: The walkers return to the trailhead. A new card in the backpack reads: Water for there and back.
lesson.beat.turnback.body1: They head home without seeing the lake. Alfredo is disappointed. So is his dad.
lesson.beat.turnback.body2: But they learned something useful for next time: bring enough water for there and back.
lesson.beat.turnback.heading: Turning back isn’t giving up.
lesson.sort.done: They couldn’t choose the storm or the closed trail. They could choose how to prepare, when to turn back, what to practise and who to ask for help.

lesson.takeaway.add.heading: Choices add up.
lesson.takeaway.add.text: Small things you repeat can grow into something big—for better or worse. One hard day doesn’t decide your future.
lesson.takeaway.build.heading: Learning builds on learning.
lesson.takeaway.build.text: What you know gives the next thing a place to start, sometimes even in something new.
lesson.takeaway.weather.heading: Not everything is yours to choose.
lesson.takeaway.weather.text: When plans change, you can pause, ask for help and find another way forward.
